50525573.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant Shigella dysenteriae type 1 Shiga toxin A subunit by SPR method

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface Plasmon: 4.3. Surface Plasmon Resonance Analysis. The interaction between small molecules inhibitors and rStx A was further explored using a ProteOn XPR36 instrument (Bio-Rad, Hercules, CA). This instrument provides real-time data of 36 simultaneous interactions in one experiment. The instrument features six injection needles with the ability to use the horizontal for six ligand immobilization conditions and vertical for six concentrations/analytes orientations of the fluidics of the sensor chip. Standard amine coupling chemistry was used to immobilize recombinant Stx A (25 μg/mL in 10 mM sodium acetate buffer, pH 5.0) on the EDAC/Sulfo-NHS [1-ethyl-3-[3-dimethylaminopropyl]carbodiimide (EDAC) and N-hydroxysulfosuccinimide (Sulfo-NHS)] activated GLH sensor chip at a density of ~6000 resonance units (RU) as per the manufacturer’s instructions. Small molecules were prepared in phosphate buffered saline–Tween 20 (PBST) and compounds were injected at 100 μL/min for 200 s at concentrations of 25.00–1.625 μM. The dissociation was monitored for 600 s. Chip surfaces were regenerated by injecting 50 mM NaOH for 30 s for reuse. All the SPR experiments were performed at 25 °C. The sensogram data obtained were analyzed using ProteOn Manager 3.1 software and fitted to the simplest Langmuir 1:1 interaction model.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 Caption: Figure 3. Surface plasmon resonance experiments to analyze the binding curves and fitted results of compound 3 to immobilized rStx A on GLH sensor chip. The concentrations of compound used were ranging from 25.00 to 1.625 μM. PBS with Tween-20 was used as a control. The data were fitted to the simplest Langmuir 1:1 interaction model. The inset is showing the association rate (ka), dissociation rate (kd), and equilibrium dissociation constant binding (KD) constants.
original_paragraph.Results Section - Binding Studies: To quantitatively assess the binding affinity of compounds 3, 4, 15, and 16 with Stx, we performed SPR experiments using immobilized rStx A on GLH sensor chips at ~6000 RU (resonance units) as described in Experimental Section. As shown in Figure 3, compound 3 binds to rStx A in a concentration dependent manner with high affinity and yielding an equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) of 7.16 × 10⁻⁷ M with a fast on rate (ka = 9.46 × 10³ 1/(M s)) and fast off rate (kd = 6.77 × 10⁻³ 1/s). Other compounds 4, 15, and 16 also interacted with Stx A but comparatively with lower affinities yielding KD values of 3.09 × 10⁻⁶, 9.68 × 10⁻⁷, and 8.67 × 10⁻² M, respectively (Figure S3).
